name: Canaries Dashboard
aliases: Canaries in the Coal Mine? Six Facts about the Recent Employment Effects of Artificial Intelligence

names: the idiom 'canary in a coal mine' (also 'canary in the coalmine', 'canary in the mine'; Cambridge Dictionary, B6): something that gives an early warning of danger or failure, from the miners' practice; Wikipedia's 'Sentinel species', section 'Canaries' (F53)
homonyms.basis: One homonym, the idiom the entity's title borrows (F13, F18, F35; CAP-1-05, CAP-1-06). At the bare name the Overview composed the idiom (T1-1–T1-8) and carried the entity as one instance of it (T1-9; CAP-1-02, CAP-1-07); cards 2–10 are the idiom's (B2–B10), recorded with their sense. The idiom is a distinct entity, never a sense of the entity's name; Wikipedia keeps the two apart (the idiom's titles redirect to 'Sentinel species'; the entity has no article).
distinct_entities: the Anthropic Economic Index (the census's relation 'uses': exposure measure and automation and augmentation ratios; the census's own entity anthropic-economic-index, https://www.laborvector.org/aggregators/anthropic-economic-index/)
Eloundou et al. (2024), the other exposure measure
ADP Research and ADP's National Employment Report (the data partner; the dashboard's sampling differs from the report's)
the Lab's other AI Economic Indicators (Transformation Tracker, Adoption Monitor, GDP-B: Surplus Observer), named on B11
the Yale Budget Lab AI tracker (the census's other observed tracker in the worked question 'observed-or-estimated', LV-31)
the February 2026 update 'Canaries, Interest Rates, and Timing: More on the Recent Drivers of Employment Changes for Young Workers' and the authors' notes, publications of the same line (F15)

T1: the idiom composed as the entity at the bare name: 'A "canary in a coal mine" is an early warning sign or indicator of hidden danger, trouble, or failure.' (T1-1), with T1-2–T1-8; the entity one bullet under 'Technology & Labor' (T1-9)
